notes: Template: TBox revision. The rule is the defining fact of the class (a fjord is a glacially carved valley flooded by the sea), held by every model and with no real exception, so the original answers are right. The revision swaps the agent for a river; that is counterfactual, which is fine. The three derived queries name a real but little-known fjord and ask what carved it (inheritance, 2 hops: the edited rule plus the membership the prompt states). The prompts give no county, country or region, so they do not invite a second, more specific stored rule ("Norway's fjords were carved by Ice Age glaciers"). Residual risk, recorded rather than removed: two names are Norwegian, and a model that knows they are in Norway could reach "a glacier" through a regional rule instead of the class rule. Dolma states that regional rule rarely as a sentence ("fjords of Norway were carved": 6; "Norwegian fjords were carved": 2), though Norway, fjords and glaciers co-occur often ("Norway AND fjords AND glaciers": about 26,600), and every fjord region is glacial, so no fjord avoids it entirely. Well-known fjords (the Sognefjord, Geirangerfjord) are not asked, since a model may hold their origin by name; for these three, Dolma has no sentence giving their origin and no co-occurrence of the name with "glacier". The third is an application: it asks an open plan question (what kind of place to visit) without naming the options, so the new answer is not in the prompt and there is no 50% floor. Near unrelated: another glacial landform under the same relation; an edit that spreads to glacial landforms in general would answer "a river" there, so it catches over-application (its reference differs from the new answer). Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the propositional side facts need checks.
